notes: internal/adapters/pop3/client.go:174 mutation-verified, not just read: removing the charge+bound block makes both endless tests fail by timeout (go test -timeout 60s -> 'panic: test timed out after 1m0s'), and setting listLineOverhead=0 hangs TestPOP3EndlessBlankLinesDiscardSession alone while the 22-byte-line test still passes. The tests therefore pin both the bound and the empty-line bypass the IMAP review (5145007) was about. Unmutated run: 3 pass in 3.18s with -race.

internal/adapters/pop3/client.go:174 the bound is on bytes, not time, so the commit subject ('cannot hold the session for ever') overstates it: deadline() still runs inside the loop, so a server that drips one line just under the 60s command timeout needs ~1.86M blank lines (32 MiB / 18 charged bytes) to trip the bound and can stretch that arbitrarily. Not a reject -- the accepted IMAP precedent (maxResponseBytes, v0.23.7) has the identical property and moving deadline() was an operator-excluded change -- but a per-command wall-clock budget is the follow-up idea, and release notes should not claim a time bound.

internal/adapters/pop3/client.go:23 the constant comment says maxListBytes 'caps how much of one multi-line response readList may accumulate', which is broader than what holds: charging happens only after textproto.ReadLine returns a whole line, and POP3 has no counterpart to IMAP's maxLineBytes (client.go:157), so one unterminated line can still accumulate unbounded bytes inside a single 60s window. Pre-existing and explicitly deferred by the implementer; worth narrowing the wording or filing the single-line bound as the next idea.

internal/adapters/pop3/client.go:230 retrBody() keeps the same unbounded shape with no body cap and still ignores domain.POP3DialOptions.MaxMessageBytes. Correctly left alone (unmerged 04b15be / PR #22 ownership, operator-excluded), but the POP3 adapter is only half-closed after this change -- do not let the release notes imply otherwise.

internal/application/sync.go:198-215 consumer behaviour checked by hand, no data loss: UIDL tripping the bound leaves uidlSupported=false, the List fallback fails on the closed socket and the job ends JobFailed/providerListFailed. The worse shape is UIDL ok + LIST tripping the bound at :208 -- lerr is silently dropped, every remote[i].Size stays 0 (so the MaxMessageBytes oversize check at :258 cannot fire), and every subsequent ingestOne fails on the dead socket and is counted stats.Failed while the job still completes. Newly reachable through this path but a pre-existing sync.go shape; confirmed DeleteAfterFetch is absent from the sync path (sync.go:31), so nothing is removed server-side.

internal/adapters/pop3/client.go:180 the implementer's own doubt confirmed: discarding via s.conn.Close() with no `broken` sentinel means later commands fail with 'use of closed network connection', so an operator reading logs sees a socket error rather than the bound that caused it. IMAP's abandon()/errUnframed carries the cause forward; consider matching it if POP3 grows a second bound.

Security (non-blocking, no attack path): no new endpoint, identifier, secret, dependency, crypto or privilege change. The only actor is the remote POP3 server, which already controls its own side; the change strictly reduces a remote memory/liveness DoS. The error string carries no line content, so no maildrop metadata reaches logs.

Legal/privacy (non-blocking): no new personal data collected, stored, transmitted or retained; no logging of message content or UIDs; no new dependency or copied code, so no license exposure; no external-facing commitment in the text.
Scope is clean -- 2 files, +296/-0, no refactor, format, dependency, migration, workflow or config-key drift. Frontend untouched, so no internal/transport/spa/assets regeneration is owed.

Verified here: go build ./..., go vet ./internal/adapters/pop3/, gofmt -l ./cmd ./internal (clean), go test -count=1 ./internal/... (all 23 packages ok, application 35.7s), go test -race on the pop3 package, and the two mutations above. NOT run: gosec/make lint-security, govulncheck, the web/ toolchain, external PostgreSQL (POSTRA_TEST_PG), and browser/PDF checks -- treat those as unverified.

For the release role: docs/releases/ has no entry for this bound yet (89aecc9 did the equivalent for IMAP v0.23.7). Describe it as a byte bound on one POP3 multi-line enumeration response, not as a timeout fix, and say retrBody remains unbounded.
